Article 45. Sectoral Responsibilities

The sectors and institutions involved, and the regional and local governments, in addition to adopting mechanisms for permanent training, capacity building and specialization, in accordance with their organic laws and other applicable regulations, are responsible for:(*)

(*) Paragraph modified by Article 1 of Law No. 30862, published on October 25, 2018, the text of which is as follows:

"The sectors and institutions involved, and the regional and local governments, in addition to adopting mechanisms for permanent training, capacity building and specialization, in accordance with their organic laws and other applicable regulations, are responsible for:"
1.	The Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations

a)	Promote and coordinate multisectoral and intergovernmental articulation actions.

b)	Provide technical advice to the different public entities so that they develop actions to eradicate violence against women and members of the family group in accordance with their competencies and functions.

c)	Promote at subnational levels of government policies, programs and projects for prevention, care and treatment such as temporary shelter homes, counseling services, mutual aid groups, Residential Care Centers, Women's Emergency Centers, Child and Adolescent Ombudsman Offices and treatment services for aggressors, among others.

d)	Supervise the implementation of the policy for prevention, protection and care of violence against women and members of the family group.
e)	Promote dissemination campaigns on the problem of violence against women and members of the family group and dissemination of the scope of this Law.
f)	Promote the study and research on the causes of violence against women and members of the family group and take measures for its correction.
g)	Promote the active participation of organizations dedicated to the protection of the rights of women, girls, boys and adolescents, older adults and persons with disabilities, among others, and the private sector, with special emphasis on the business sector, in programs for prevention, care and recovery from violence against women and members of the family group.

h)	Arrange the necessary measures in order to implement prevention and care actions for victims of violence in rural areas of the country and with respect to victims in greater situations of vulnerability.

2.	The Ministry of Education

a)	Supervise compliance with public policy guidelines against violence against women and members of the family group, within the scope of its competence.
b)	Strengthen at all educational modalities and levels the teaching of ethical values oriented to respect for the dignity of the person within the framework of the right to live free from violence, eliminating stereotypes that exacerbate, tolerate or legitimize violence, inferiority or subordination in the family group, especially those that affect women.

c)	Supervise that in all educational materials sexist or discriminatory stereotypes are eliminated and, on the contrary, the equality of men and women is promoted.
d)	Promote and strengthen programs for schools for parents; and for preparation for life and

healthy coexistence in the family group; establishing mechanisms for the detection and referral to the institutions of the System, of cases of violence against women and members of the family group.
e)	Implement in educational institutions of Regular Basic Education (EBR) and Alternative Basic Education (EBA), contents of the National Curricular Design (DCN) on respect for the right to a life free from violence, with active methodologies and evaluation systems that adapt to the various cultural, ethnic and linguistic contexts.

f)	Implement capacity strengthening programs in initial and ongoing teacher training on the themes of the struggle to eradicate violence against women and members of the family group, incorporating in guides, modules and teacher training programs, topics such as types of violence, gender socialization and violence, identification of risk factors related to violence and mechanisms for strengthening support networks for prevention.

g)	Disseminate the problem of sexual harassment among teaching and administrative staff, as well as the sector's protocols.
h)	Incorporate in guides directed to the school population, content on prevention of harassment and sexual abuse in girls and boys.
i)	Implement creative and impactful strategies on the fight against violence against women and members of the family group, in non-formal educational spaces such as markets, recreational spaces, bus terminals, waiting rooms of public and private institutions, among others.

3.	The Ministry of Health

a)	Promote and strengthen programs for the promotion, protection, recovery and rehabilitation of health, contributing to achieving the well-being and development of the person, in conditions of full accessibility and respect for fundamental rights, in accordance with sectoral policies.

b)	Guarantee quality care for cases of violence against women and members of the family group, including their affiliation in the Comprehensive Health Insurance for free comprehensive physical and mental health care and recovery, which includes care, examinations, hospitalization, medications, psychological or psychiatric treatment and any other activity necessary for the restoration of health.

c)	Develop awareness and continuous training programs for health personnel in order to improve and promote adequate care for victims of violence referred to in the law.

4.	The Ministry of the Interior

a)	Establish, through its line, support and control bodies, the guidelines and technical guidelines for the adequate execution, supervision and control of the provisions for prevention, care and protection against violence against women and members of the family group, in compliance with the functions of the interior sector, with special participation of the Executive Directorate of Citizen Security of the National Police of Peru as the specialized technical body in receiving complaints and investigating cases of violence against women and members of the family group.

b)	Promote, in the National Police of Peru, the creation of functional specialization in matters of violence against women and members of the family group. The Executive Directorate of Citizen Security is the specialized body responsible for the organization, specialization and performance evaluation.

c)	Implement, in coordination with the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations, the Modules for Attention to Women Victims of Family and Sexual Violence, provided for in Supreme Decree 012-2013-IN as a national policy of the Peruvian State.

d)	Guarantee in police station services and competent areas the permanence of specialized and sensitized personnel.

e)	Provide timely attention for the implementation and compliance with protection measures granted by the Public Prosecutor's Office to persons affected by violence against women and members of the family group.

f)	Issue standard forms to facilitate complaints and regulate the necessary police procedures to ensure the diligent referral of actions taken on complaints received to family courts or equivalent within the time period established in this Law.

g)	Prepare pamphlets and other instruments for mass dissemination for the adequate care of victims of violence against women and members of the family group in police stations and police dependencies.(*)

(*) Subsection modified by Article 1 of Law No. 30862, published on October 25, 2018, the text of which is as follows:

"4. The Ministry of the Interior

a)	Establish, through its line, support and control bodies, the guidelines and technical guidelines for the adequate execution, supervision and control of the provisions for prevention, care and protection against violence against women and members of the family group, in compliance with the functions of the interior sector, through a specialized high-level instance that links the Criminal Investigation area and the Prevention, Order and Security area of the National Police of Peru.

b)	Promote in the National Police of Peru the creation of Family and Violence against Women and Family Group sections that are responsible for receiving and investigating all complaints of misdemeanors and crimes that arise within the framework of this law in police stations nationwide. Likewise, convert the existing specialized police stations to date to this competence.

c)	Implement, in coordination with the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations, the Modules for Attention to Women Victims of Family and Sexual Violence, provided for in the National Citizen Security Plan as a national policy of the Peruvian State.

d)	Guarantee the existence of police personnel duly trained in matters of rights of women and members of the family group, in order to provide adequate attention to cases of violence against women and members of the family group, in police station services and competent areas, who in order to safeguard the privacy and psychological integrity of the victim will be in charge of receiving the corresponding complaints and carrying out interrogations of the aggressor and the victim, among other functions determined by law and its regulations, under administrative, civil or criminal liability, in case of non-compliance. If the victim prefers to be attended by female personnel, it must be guaranteed that she is attended by such duly trained personnel.

e)	Provide timely and priority attention for the implementation and compliance with protection measures granted to persons affected by violence against women and members of the family group.
f)	Issue standard forms to facilitate complaints and regulate the necessary police procedures to ensure the diligent referral of actions taken on complaints received to family courts or

equivalent within the time period established in this law.

g)	Prepare pamphlets and other instruments for mass dissemination for the adequate care of victims of violence against women and members of the family group in police stations and police dependencies in coordination with the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations.

h)	Provide training to members of the National Police of Peru on matters of violence against women and members of the family group, in coordination with the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations.

i)	Investigate and disciplinarily sanction acts of violence against women and members of the family group committed by its civilian personnel and police personnel.
j)	Make effective compliance with the prohibition of possession and carrying of weapons ordered through protection measures, with respect to its civilian and police personnel."
5.	The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights

a)	Systematize and disseminate the legal system of the State in matters of the struggle to eradicate violence against women and members of the family group.
b)	Provide public defense service to victims of violence against women and members of the family group.
c)	Provide, through the National Penitentiary Institute, differentiated penitentiary treatment for persons sentenced for acts of violence against women and members of the family group.

6.	The Ministry of Labor and Employment Promotion

a)	Prioritize, within the framework of programs, strategies and action plans for employment promotion and employability, the care of victims of violence for their incorporation into the labor market as employees or through the development of productive self-employment and other forms of entrepreneurship.

b)	Coordinate with the pertinent instances in order to guarantee compliance with the provisions of this Law regarding labor rights of workers who are victims of violence.

7.	The Ministry of Transportation and Communications
Ensure strict compliance with the obligations of the media established in this Law.
8.	The Ministry of Economy and Finance
Allocate the necessary resources for compliance with this Law.

9.	The Ministry of Development and Social Inclusion

a)	Incorporate, in programs attached to the Ministry of Development and Social Inclusion, persons affected by violence against women and members of the family group, provided that the criteria and rules established in current regulations are met.

b)	Make available to society information regarding the execution of social programs

that have benefited persons affected by violence against women and members of the family group.

10.	The Ministry of Defense
Incorporate in the educational guidelines of the Armed Forces specific content against violence against women and members of the family group in accordance with the approaches provided for in this Law, as well as in its academic bodies and attached public agencies.(*)

(*) Subsection modified by Article 1 of Law No. 30862, published on October 25, 2018, the text of which is as follows:

"10. The Ministry of Defense

a)	Incorporate in the educational guidelines of the Armed Forces specific content against violence against women and members of the family group in accordance with the approaches provided for in this law, as well as in its academic bodies and attached public agencies.

b)	Investigate and disciplinarily sanction acts of violence against women and members of the family group, committed by its civilian personnel and military personnel.
c)	Make effective compliance with the prohibition of possession and carrying of weapons ordered through protection measures, with respect to its civilian and military personnel."
11.	The Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Formulate, coordinate, execute and evaluate the policy of protection and assistance of nationals abroad for cases of violence against women and members of the family group.

12.	The Judicial Branch
Administer justice, respecting the rights to due process and procedural economy and speed in cases of violence against women and members of the family group. All proceedings before the Judicial Branch in matters of violence against women and members of the family group are free for victims.(*)

(*) Subsection modified by Article 1 of Law No. 30862, published on October 25, 2018, the text of which is as follows:

"12. The Judicial Branch
Administer justice, respecting the rights to due process and procedural economy and speed in cases of violence against women and members of the family group. All proceedings before the Judicial Branch in matters of violence against women and members of the family group are free for victims; and ensure permanent and specialized training of judges on issues of violence against women and members of the family group."

13.	The Public Prosecutor's Office
Prepare, through the Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences, guides and protocols for scientific-forensic activity and in judicial processes, being responsible for their dissemination in order to standardize care and assessment criteria.(*)

(*) Subsection modified by Article 1 of Law No. 30862, published on October 25, 2018, the text of which is as follows:

"13. The Public Prosecutor's Office
Prepare, through the Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences, guides and protocols for

scientific-forensic activity and in judicial processes, being responsible for their dissemination in order to standardize care and assessment criteria; and ensure permanent and specialized training of prosecutors and forensic physicians on issues of violence against women and members of the family group."
14.	Regional and local governments

a)	Formulate policies, regulate, direct, execute, promote, supervise and control regional, local and community plans, policies and programs, to raise awareness, prevent, detect and address all forms of violence against women and members of the family group.

b)	Those established in this Law.(*)

(*) Subsection 14) modified by Article 2 of Legislative Decree No. 1386, published on September 4, 2018, the text of which is as follows:

"14. Regional and local governments

14.1	In the case of regional governments

a)	Formulate policies, regulate, direct, execute, promote, supervise and control regional plans, policies and programs, to raise awareness, prevent, detect and address all forms of violence against women and members of the family group.

b)	Create and lead regional coordination instances, to promote the articulation and functioning of the National System in their jurisdiction.
c)	Incorporate in their citizen security plans actions for prevention and fight against violence against women and members of the family group, as well as monitoring of the effectiveness of such actions in the coordination spaces of the Regional Citizen Security Committees.
d)	Those established in this Law.

14.2	In the case of local governments

a)	Formulate policies, regulate, direct, execute, promote, supervise and control local and community plans, policies and programs, to raise awareness, prevent, detect and address all forms of violence against women and members of the family group.

b)	Create and lead provincial and district coordination instances, to promote the articulation and functioning of the National System in their jurisdiction.
c)	Implement care, reeducation and treatment services for aggressors, with the approaches established in this law.
d)	Implement prevention services against violence against women and members of the family group, through actions of social and economic empowerment of victims of violence and preventive programs, reflection groups directed at men to promote egalitarian relationships free from violence.

e)	Incorporate in their citizen security plans actions for prevention and fight against violence against women and members of the family group, as well as monitoring of the effectiveness of such

actions in the coordination spaces of the Provincial Citizen Security Committees and District Citizen Security Committees.

f)	Those established in this Law."

15.	National Superintendence for Control of Security Services, Arms, Ammunition and Explosives for Civilian Use (SUCAMEC)
a)	Request sworn statement of not having a record of family violence in applications for firearms licenses.
b)	Seize weapons that are in the possession of persons with respect to whom the suspension of the right to possession and carrying of weapons has been ordered.
c)	Void the license for possession and use of weapons due to supervening record of family violence.
d)	Submit semi-annually updated information to the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations, corresponding to the number of licenses canceled and weapons seized for acts of violence against women and members of the family group.

"16.National Council of the Magistracy (CNM)
Incorporate in the Regulations for Open Access Competitions in the Selection and Appointment of Judges and Prosecutors, as well as in the Regulations for Promotions and for Evaluation and Ratification, as a prior and mandatory requirement, that applicants have academic training in matters of violence against women and members of the family group, human rights and interculturality related to women and members of the family group, through programs, workshops, training or others defined by the regulations."(*)

(*) Subsection 16) incorporated by Article 1 of Law No. 30862, published on October 25, 2018.

heading: Article 46. General obligations of the media
text:
Artículo 46. Obligaciones generales de los medios de comunicación

Los medios de comunicación, en la difusión de informaciones relativas a la violencia sobre la mujer garantizan, con la correspondiente objetividad informativa, la defensa de los derechos humanos, la libertad y dignidad de las mujeres víctimas de violencia y de sus hijos. En particular, tienen especial cuidado en el tratamiento gráfico de las informaciones.
Los servicios de radiodifusión públicos y privados permiten el uso de la franja educativa del 10% de su programación para que, en el horario de protección familiar, las instituciones públicas articuladas en el Sistema Nacional para la Prevención, Sanción y Erradicación de la Violencia contra las Mujeres y los Integrantes del Grupo Familiar desarrollen contenidos vinculados a la sensibilización, prevención, atención, protección, sanción y reeducación para la erradicación de la violencia contra las mujeres y los integrantes del grupo familiar.
translated_text:
Article 46. General obligations of the media

The media, in the dissemination of information related to violence against women, guarantee, with the corresponding informative objectivity, the defense of human rights, the freedom and dignity of women victims of violence and their children. In particular, they take special care in the graphic treatment of information.
Public and private broadcasting services allow the use of the educational segment of 10% of their programming so that, during family protection hours, the public institutions articulated in the National System for the Prevention, Punishment and Eradication of Violence against Women and Members of the Family Group develop content related to awareness, prevention, care, protection, punishment and re-education for the eradication of violence against women and members of the family group.

heading: Article 47. Intervention of indigenous or native peoples
text:
Artículo 47. Intervención de los pueblos indígenas u originarios

La intervención de los pueblos indígenas u originarios en casos de violencia contra las mujeres y los integrantes del grupo familiar se sujeta a lo dispuesto en el artículo 149 de la Constitución Política.(*)

(*) Artículo modificado por el Artículo 1 de la Ley N° 30862, publicada el 25 octubre 2018, cuyo texto es el siguiente:

"Artículo 47. Intervención de los pueblos indígenas u originarios y justicia en zonas

rurales
Los casos de violencia contra las mujeres y los integrantes del grupo familiar que se produzcan
en territorio de comunidades campesinas, comunidades nativas y rondas campesinas, serán conocidos por sus autoridades jurisdiccionales según lo previsto en el artículo 149 de la Constitución Política.
En las localidades donde no exista juzgado de familia o juzgado de paz letrado con competencia delegada, los actos de violencia contra las mujeres y los integrantes del grupo familiar son de competencia del juzgado de paz, debiendo observarse lo previsto en la Ley 29824, Ley de Justicia de Paz, y su reglamento.

Cuando el juzgado de paz toma conocimiento de actos de violencia contra las mujeres y los integrantes del grupo familiar dicta las medidas de protección que correspondan a favor de la víctima. El Poder Judicial, con cargo a su presupuesto institucional, asume los costos en los que incurran los juzgados de paz para poner en conocimiento de lo actuado al juzgado de familia y a la fiscalía penal o mixta, y para realizar notificaciones u exhortos.

En los centros poblados donde no exista comisaría, los juzgados de paz coordinan la ejecución de las medidas de protección y las sanciones impuestas con las autoridades de las comunidades campesinas, comunidades nativas o rondas campesinas.

Los servicios de salud aseguran la promoción, prevención, atención y recuperación integral de la salud física y mental de las víctimas de acuerdo a lo dispuesto por los juzgados de paz y/o las autoridades de las comunidades campesinas, comunidades nativas o rondas campesinas, de conformidad con lo establecido en el artículo 10, literal c), de la presente ley."

DISPOSICIONES COMPLEMENTARIAS FINALES

PRIMERA. Reglamentación
El reglamento de la presente Ley se expide por el Poder Ejecutivo en un plazo no mayor a noventa días calendario desde su entrada en vigencia. Para tal efecto, se convoca a una comisión conformada por el Ministerio de Justicia y Derechos Humanos, el Ministerio de la Mujer y Poblaciones Vulnerables, el Ministerio del Interior, el Poder Judicial y el Ministerio Público.

SEGUNDA. Prevalencia normativa
Las disposiciones de esta Ley prevalecen sobre otras normas generales o especiales que se les opongan. Los derechos que reconoce la presente Ley a las víctimas de violencia hacia la mujer y contra los integrantes del grupo familiar son irrenunciables.

TERCERA. Implementación del Observatorio Nacional de la Violencia contra las Mujeres y los Integrantes del Grupo Familiar y del Centro de Altos Estudios
La implementación del Observatorio Nacional de la Violencia contra las Mujeres y los Integrantes del Grupo Familiar y del Centro de Altos Estudios contra la Violencia contra las Mujeres y los Integrantes del Grupo Familiar, a que se refieren los artículos 43 y 44 de la presente Ley, estará sujeto a la disponibilidad presupuestal que para tal efecto disponga el Ministerio de la Mujer y Poblaciones Vulnerables.
“Cuarta. Referencia a juzgados, salas y fiscalías de familia
Cuando la presente ley hace referencia a los juzgados, salas y fiscalías de familia, debe entenderse que comprende a los juzgados, salas y fiscalías que hagan sus veces.”(*)
(*) Disposición incorporada por el Artículo 3 del Decreto Legislativo N° 1386, publicado el 04 septiembre 2018.

“Quinta. Publicación sobre cumplimiento de plazos
El Poder Judicial publica anualmente en su portal institucional información sobre el cumplimiento de los plazos para el dictado de las medidas de protección, por parte de los juzgados de familia.”(*)
(*) Disposición incorporada por el Artículo 3 del Decreto Legislativo N° 1386, publicado el 04 septiembre 2018.

"SEXTA. Informes
La Presidencia del Consejo de Ministros, en el marco del “25 de noviembre, Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra la Mujer”, presenta un informe respecto al avance en el cumplimiento de la Ley 30364, Ley para Prevenir, Sancionar y Erradicar la Violencia contra las Mujeres y los Integrantes del Grupo Familiar, con especial énfasis en la implementación del Sistema Nacional previsto en dicha norma.
Para dar cumplimiento a ello, los ministerios y demás entidades integrantes del Sistema remiten la información correspondiente al Ministerio de la Mujer y Poblaciones Vulnerables, bajo responsabilidad del titular del pliego."(*)

(*) Disposición incorporada por el Artículo 2 de la Ley N° 30862, publicada el 25 octubre 2018.

DISPOSICIONES COMPLEMENTARIAS TRANSITORIAS

PRIMERA. Procesos en trámite
Los procesos que se encuentren en trámite continuarán rigiéndose bajo las normas con que se iniciaron hasta su conclusión.

SEGUNDA. Comisión Especial
Créase la Comisión Especial para el diseño, conducción, coordinación, supervisión y evaluación del proceso de adecuación del Sistema Nacional para la Prevención, Sanción y Erradicación de la Violencia contra las Mujeres y los Integrantes del Grupo Familiar a la presente Ley.

TERCERA. Integrantes de la Comisión Especial
La Comisión señalada en la disposición complementaria transitoria segunda está integrada por seis miembros:	El titular del Ministerio de la Mujer y Poblaciones Vulnerables o su representante, quien la presidirá.	El titular del Ministerio de Justicia y Derechos Humanos o su representante.
El titular del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas o su representante.
El titular del Ministerio del Interior o su representante.
El titular del Poder Judicial o su representante.
El titular del Ministerio Público o su representante.

CUARTA. Atribuciones de la Comisión Especial
Las atribuciones de la Comisión Especial son las siguientes:

1.	Formular las políticas y objetivos para la adecuación progresiva de la Ley.

2.	Diseñar la propuesta del Plan de Adecuación del Sistema de Justicia al Sistema Nacional para la Prevención, Sanción y Erradicación de la Violencia contra las Mujeres y los Integrantes del Grupo Familiar.

3.	Elaborar los anteproyectos de normas que sean necesarios para la transferencia de los recursos presupuestarios a que hubiere lugar.
4.	Establecer, en coordinación con las entidades vinculadas, los programas anuales de adecuación, provisión de recursos materiales y humanos que permitan la ejecución del Plan de Adecuación del Sistema de Justicia a la Ley.
5.	Concordar, supervisar y efectuar un seguimiento y evaluación de la ejecución de los planes y programas de adecuación a la Ley.

6.	Elaborar informes semestrales, los cuales son remitidos a la Comisión Multisectorial de Alto
Nivel.

QUINTA. Plazo
El plazo para la formulación del Plan de Adecuación del Sistema de Justicia por la Comisión es de sesenta días hábiles contados a partir de la instalación de la misma. Asimismo, el plazo para que la citada comisión culmine sus funciones es de ciento ochenta días hábiles a partir de la instalación de la misma.

"SEXTA. Diseño de programa presupuestal multisectorial
El Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, a través de la Dirección General de Presupuesto Público, acompaña al Ministerio de la Mujer y Poblaciones Vulnerables, que preside el Sistema Nacional para la Prevención, Sanción y Erradicación de la Violencia contra las Mujeres y los Integrantes del Grupo Familiar, en el diseño de un programa presupuestal multisectorial para la implementación de dicho sistema, así como los indicadores para su respectivo seguimiento de desempeño, evaluaciones e incentivos a la gestión a que hubiera lugar, en el plazo de ciento ochenta días hábiles desde la vigencia de la Ley.

En atención a la naturaleza del Sistema Nacional, el programa presupuestal debe involucrar por lo menos al Ministerio de la Mujer y Poblaciones Vulnerables, Ministerio de Justicia y Derechos Humanos, Ministerio del Interior, Poder Judicial, Ministerio Público y a los tres niveles de gobierno."(*)

(*) Disposición incorporada por el Artículo 2 de la Ley N° 30862, publicada el 25 octubre 2018.

DISPOSICIONES COMPLEMENTARIAS MODIFICATORIAS

PRIMERA. Modificación de los artículos 45, 121-A, 121-B, 122, 377 y 378 del Código Penal
Modifícanse los artículos 45, 121-A, 121-B, 122, 377 y 378 del Código Penal en los siguientes términos:

“Artículo 45. Presupuestos para fundamentar y determinar la pena
El juez, al momento de fundamentar y determinar la pena, tiene en cuenta:

a.	Las carencias sociales que hubiese sufrido el agente o el abuso de su cargo, posición económica, formación, poder, oficio, profesión o la función que ocupe en la sociedad.

b.	Su cultura y sus costumbres.

c.	Los intereses de la víctima, de su familia o de las personas que de ella dependan, así como la afectación de sus derechos y considerando especialmente su situación de vulnerabilidad.
translated_text:
Article 47. Intervention of indigenous or native peoples

The intervention of indigenous or native peoples in cases of violence against women and members of the family group is subject to the provisions of article 149 of the Political Constitution.(*)

(*) Article modified by Article 1 of Law No. 30862, published on October 25, 2018, whose text is as follows:

"Article 47. Intervention of indigenous or native peoples and justice in rural areas

Cases of violence against women and members of the family group that occur in the territory of peasant communities, native communities and peasant patrols, shall be heard by their jurisdictional authorities as provided in article 149 of the Political Constitution.
In localities where there is no family court or justice of the peace court with delegated jurisdiction, acts of violence against women and members of the family group are within the jurisdiction of the justice of the peace court, and the provisions of Law 29824, Justice of the Peace Law, and its regulations must be observed.

When the justice of the peace court becomes aware of acts of violence against women and members of the family group, it issues the appropriate protection measures in favor of the victim. The Judicial Branch, charged to its institutional budget, assumes the costs incurred by the justice of the peace courts to notify the family court and the criminal or mixed prosecutor's office of the actions taken, and to carry out notifications or letters rogatory.

In populated centers where there is no police station, the justice of the peace courts coordinate the execution of protection measures and sanctions imposed with the authorities of the peasant communities, native communities or peasant patrols.

Health services ensure the promotion, prevention, care and comprehensive recovery of the physical and mental health of victims in accordance with the provisions of the justice of the peace courts and/or the authorities of the peasant communities, native communities or peasant patrols, in accordance with the provisions of article 10, paragraph c), of this law."

FINAL COMPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

FIRST. Regulation
The regulations of this Law shall be issued by the Executive Branch within a period not exceeding ninety calendar days from its entry into force. For this purpose, a commission is convened consisting of the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations, the Ministry of the Interior, the Judicial Branch and the Public Prosecutor's Office.

SECOND. Normative prevalence
The provisions of this Law prevail over other general or special rules that oppose them. The rights that this Law recognizes to victims of violence against women and against members of the family group are non-waivable.

THIRD. Implementation of the National Observatory on Violence against Women and Members of the Family Group and the Center for Advanced Studies
The implementation of the National Observatory on Violence against Women and Members of the Family Group and the Center for Advanced Studies against Violence against Women and Members of the Family Group, referred to in articles 43 and 44 of this Law, shall be subject to the budgetary availability that the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations provides for this purpose.
"Fourth. Reference to family courts, chambers and prosecutor's offices
When this law refers to family courts, chambers and prosecutor's offices, it should be understood to include the courts, chambers and prosecutor's offices that serve in their place."(*)
(*) Provision incorporated by Article 3 of Legislative Decree No. 1386, published on September 4, 2018.

"Fifth. Publication on compliance with deadlines
The Judicial Branch publishes annually on its institutional portal information on compliance with deadlines for the issuance of protection measures by family courts."(*)
(*) Provision incorporated by Article 3 of Legislative Decree No. 1386, published on September 4, 2018.

"SIXTH. Reports
The Presidency of the Council of Ministers, within the framework of "November 25, International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women", presents a report regarding progress in compliance with Law 30364, Law to Prevent, Punish and Eradicate Violence against Women and Members of the Family Group, with special emphasis on the implementation of the National System provided for in said law.
To comply with this, the ministries and other entities that are part of the System send the corresponding information to the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations, under the responsibility of the head of the budget."(*)

(*) Provision incorporated by Article 2 of Law No. 30862, published on October 25, 2018.

TRANSITORY COMPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

FIRST. Proceedings in process
Proceedings that are in process shall continue to be governed by the rules under which they were initiated until their conclusion.

SECOND. Special Commission
The Special Commission is created for the design, conduct, coordination, supervision and evaluation of the process of adaptation of the National System for the Prevention, Punishment and Eradication of Violence against Women and Members of the Family Group to this Law.

THIRD. Members of the Special Commission
The Commission referred to in the second transitory complementary provision is composed of six members:	The head of the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations or his representative, who shall preside over it.	The head of the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights or his representative.
The head of the Ministry of Economy and Finance or his representative.
The head of the Ministry of the Interior or his representative.
The head of the Judicial Branch or his representative.
The head of the Public Prosecutor's Office or his representative.

FOURTH. Powers of the Special Commission
The powers of the Special Commission are as follows:

1.	Formulate policies and objectives for the progressive adaptation of the Law.

2.	Design the proposal for the Plan for Adaptation of the Justice System to the National System for the Prevention, Punishment and Eradication of Violence against Women and Members of the Family Group.

3.	Prepare draft regulations that are necessary for the transfer of budgetary resources as appropriate.
4.	Establish, in coordination with the related entities, the annual adaptation programs, provision of material and human resources that allow the execution of the Plan for Adaptation of the Justice System to the Law.
5.	Coordinate, supervise and monitor and evaluate the execution of the plans and programs for adaptation to the Law.

6.	Prepare semi-annual reports, which are sent to the High-Level Multisectoral Commission.

FIFTH. Deadline
The deadline for the formulation of the Justice System Adaptation Plan by the Commission is sixty working days from the installation of the same. Likewise, the deadline for said commission to complete its functions is one hundred eighty working days from the installation of the same.

"SIXTH. Design of multisectoral budget program
The Ministry of Economy and Finance, through the General Directorate of Public Budget, accompanies the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations, which presides over the National System for the Prevention, Punishment and Eradication of Violence against Women and Members of the Family Group, in the design of a multisectoral budget program for the implementation of said system, as well as the indicators for its respective performance monitoring, evaluations and management incentives as appropriate, within one hundred eighty working days from the entry into force of the Law.

In view of the nature of the National System, the budget program must involve at least the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations, Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, Ministry of the Interior, Judicial Branch, Public Prosecutor's Office and the three levels of government."(*)

(*) Provision incorporated by Article 2 of Law No. 30862, published on October 25, 2018.

MODIFYING COMPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

FIRST. Modification of articles 45, 121-A, 121-B, 122, 377 and 378 of the Criminal Code
Articles 45, 121-A, 121-B, 122, 377 and 378 of the Criminal Code are modified as follows:

"Article 45. Prerequisites for grounding and determining the penalty
The judge, when grounding and determining the penalty, takes into account:

a.	The social deprivations that the agent may have suffered or the abuse of his position, economic position, training, power, trade, profession or the function he holds in society.

b.	His culture and his customs.

c.	The interests of the victim, of his family or of the persons who depend on him, as well as the violation of his rights and especially considering his situation of vulnerability.

heading: Article 121
text:
Artículo 121

A. Formas agravadas. Lesiones graves cuando la víctima es menor de edad, de la tercera edad o persona con discapacidad
En los casos previstos en la primera parte del artículo 121, cuando la víctima sea menor de edad, mayor de sesenta y cinco años o sufre discapacidad física o mental y el agente se aprovecha de dicha condición se aplica pena privativa de libertad no menor de seis ni mayor de doce años.
Cuando la víctima muere a consecuencia de la lesión y el agente pudo prever ese resultado, la pena será no menor de doce ni mayor de quince años. (*)

(*) Confrontar con la Única Disposición Complementaria Derogatoria del Decreto Legislativo N° 1323, publicado el 06 enero 2017.
translated_text:
Article 121

A. Aggravated forms. Serious injuries when the victim is a minor, elderly or person with disability
In the cases provided for in the first part of article 121, when the victim is a minor, over sixty-five years of age or suffers from physical or mental disability and the agent takes advantage of such condition, a custodial sentence of not less than six nor more than twelve years shall be imposed.
When the victim dies as a consequence of the injury and the agent could have foreseen that result, the sentence shall be not less than twelve nor more than fifteen years. (*)

(*) Compare with the Single Complementary Repealing Provision of Legislative Decree No. 1323, published on January 6, 2017.

heading: Article 121
text:
Artículo 121

B.- Formas agravadas. Lesiones graves por violencia contra la mujer y su entorno familiar
En los casos previstos en la primera parte del artículo 121 se aplica pena privativa de libertad no menor de seis ni mayor de doce años cuando la víctima:
1.	Es mujer y es lesionada por su condición de tal en cualquiera de los contextos previstos en el primer párrafo del artículo 108-B.
2.	Es ascendiente, descendiente, natural o adoptivo, cónyuge o conviviente del agente.

3.	Depende o está subordinado.

Cuando la víctima muere a consecuencia de la lesión y el agente pudo prever ese resultado, la pena será no menor de doce ni mayor de quince años.(*)

(*) Confrontar con el Artículo 1 del Decreto Legislativo N° 1323, publicado el 06 enero 2017.
translated_text:
Article 121

B.- Aggravated forms. Serious injuries due to violence against women and their family environment
In the cases provided for in the first part of article 121, a custodial sentence of not less than six nor more than twelve years shall be imposed when the victim:
1.	Is a woman and is injured because of her condition as such in any of the contexts provided for in the first paragraph of article 108-B.
2.	Is an ascendant, descendant, natural or adoptive, spouse or cohabitant of the agent.

3.	Is dependent or subordinate.

When the victim dies as a consequence of the injury and the agent could have foreseen that result, the sentence shall be not less than twelve nor more than fifteen years.(*)

(*) Compare with Article 1 of Legislative Decree No. 1323, published on January 6, 2017.

heading: Article 122. Minor injuries
text:
Artículo 122. Lesiones leves

1.	El que causa a otro lesiones en el cuerpo o en la salud que requiera más de diez y menos de treinta días de asistencia o descanso, o nivel moderado de daño psíquico, según prescripción facultativa, será reprimido con pena privativa de libertad no menor de dos ni mayor de cinco años.
2.	La pena será privativa de libertad no menor de seis ni mayor de doce años si la víctima muere como consecuencia de la lesión prevista en el párrafo 1 y el agente pudo prever ese resultado.
3.	La pena será privativa de libertad no menor de tres ni mayor de seis años si la víctima:

a.	Es miembro de la Policía Nacional del Perú o de las Fuerzas Armadas, magistrado del Poder Judicial, del Ministerio Público o del Tribunal Constitucional o autoridad elegida por mandato popular o funcionario o servidor público y es lesionada en el ejercicio de sus funciones oficiales o como consecuencia de ellas.

b.	Es menor de edad, mayor de sesenta y cinco años o sufre de discapacidad física o mental y el agente se aprovecha de dicha condición.

c.	Es mujer y es lesionada por su condición de tal, en cualquiera de los contextos previstos en el primer párrafo del artículo 108-B.
d.	Es ascendiente, descendiente, natural o adoptivo, cónyuge o conviviente del agente.

e.	Depende o está subordinada de cualquier forma al agente.

4.	La pena privativa de libertad será no menor de ocho ni mayor de catorce años si la víctima muere como consecuencia de la lesión a que se refiere el párrafo 3 y el agente pudo prever ese resultado.

5.	El juez impone la inhabilitación correspondiente a los supuestos previstos en el párrafo 3.() () Confrontar con el Artículo 1 del Decreto Legislativo N° 1323, publicado el 06 enero 2017.
translated_text:
Article 122. Minor injuries

1.	Whoever causes another person injuries to the body or health that require more than ten and less than thirty days of care or rest, or a moderate level of psychological damage, according to medical prescription, shall be punished with a custodial sentence of not less than two nor more than five years.
2.	The sentence shall be a custodial sentence of not less than six nor more than twelve years if the victim dies as a consequence of the injury provided for in paragraph 1 and the agent could have foreseen that result.
3.	The sentence shall be a custodial sentence of not less than three nor more than six years if the victim:

a.	Is a member of the National Police of Peru or the Armed Forces, magistrate of the Judicial Branch, the Public Prosecutor's Office or the Constitutional Court or authority elected by popular mandate or public official or servant and is injured in the exercise of their official functions or as a consequence thereof.

b.	Is a minor, over sixty-five years of age or suffers from physical or mental disability and the agent takes advantage of such condition.

c.	Is a woman and is injured because of her condition as such, in any of the contexts provided for in the first paragraph of article 108-B.
d.	Is an ascendant, descendant, natural or adoptive, spouse or cohabitant of the agent.

e.	Is dependent or subordinate in any form to the agent.

4.	The custodial sentence shall be not less than eight nor more than fourteen years if the victim dies as a consequence of the injury referred to in paragraph 3 and the agent could have foreseen that result.

5.	The judge imposes the corresponding disqualification for the cases provided for in paragraph 3.() () Compare with Article 1 of Legislative Decree No. 1323, published on January 6, 2017.

heading: Article 377. Omission, refusal or delay of official acts
text:
Artículo 377. Omisión, rehusamiento o demora de actos funcionales

El funcionario público que, ilegalmente, omite, rehúsa o retarda algún acto de su cargo será reprimido con pena privativa de libertad no mayor de dos años y con treinta a sesenta días-multa.
Cuando la omisión, rehusamiento o demora de actos funcionales esté referido a una solicitud de garantías personales o caso de violencia familiar, la pena será privativa de libertad no menor de dos ni mayor de cinco años.
translated_text:
Article 377. Omission, refusal or delay of official acts

The public official who, illegally, omits, refuses or delays any act of their office shall be punished with a custodial sentence of not more than two years and with thirty to sixty days-fine.
When the omission, refusal or delay of official acts refers to a request for personal guarantees or a case of family violence, the sentence shall be a custodial sentence of not less than two nor more than five years.

heading: Article 378. Denial or deficient police support
text:
Artículo 378. Denegación o deficiente apoyo policial

El policía que rehúsa, omite o retarda, sin causa justificada, la prestación de un auxilio legalmente requerido por la autoridad civil competente, será reprimido con pena privativa de libertad no mayor de dos años.
Si la prestación de auxilio es requerida por un particular en situación de peligro, la pena será no menor de dos ni mayor de cuatro años.
La pena prevista en el párrafo segundo se impondrá, si la prestación de auxilio está referida a una solicitud de garantías personales o un caso de violencia familiar”.

SEGUNDA. Incorporación de los artículos 46-E y 124-B al Código Penal
Incorpóranse los artículos 46-E y 124-B al Código Penal en los siguientes términos:

“Artículo 46-E. Circunstancia agravante cualificada por abuso de parentesco
La pena es aumentada hasta en un tercio por encima del máximo legal fijado para el delito cuando el agente se haya aprovechado de su calidad de ascendiente o descendiente, natural o adoptivo, padrastro o madrastra, cónyuge o conviviente de la víctima. En este caso, la pena privativa de libertad no puede exceder los treinta y cinco años, salvo que el delito se encuentre reprimido con pena privativa de libertad indeterminada, en cuyo caso se aplica esta última.
La agravante prevista en el primer párrafo es inaplicable cuando esté establecida como tal en la ley penal.
translated_text:
Article 378. Denial or deficient police support

The police officer who refuses, omits or delays, without justified cause, the provision of assistance legally required by the competent civil authority, shall be punished with a custodial sentence of not more than two years.
If the provision of assistance is required by a private individual in a situation of danger, the sentence shall be not less than two nor more than four years.
The sentence provided for in the second paragraph shall be imposed, if the provision of assistance refers to a request for personal guarantees or a case of family violence".

SECOND. Incorporation of articles 46-E and 124-B into the Criminal Code
Articles 46-E and 124-B are incorporated into the Criminal Code in the following terms:

"Article 46-E. Aggravating circumstance qualified by abuse of kinship
The sentence is increased by up to one third above the maximum legal limit set for the crime when the agent has taken advantage of their status as ascendant or descendant, natural or adoptive, stepfather or stepmother, spouse or cohabitant of the victim. In this case, the custodial sentence may not exceed thirty-five years, unless the crime is punished with an indeterminate custodial sentence, in which case the latter applies.
The aggravating circumstance provided for in the first paragraph is inapplicable when it is established as such in criminal law.

Artículo 124

B. Determinación de la lesión psicológica
El nivel de la lesión psicológica es determinado mediante valoración realizada de conformidad con el instrumento técnico oficial especializado que orienta la labor pericial, con la siguiente equivalencia:

a.	Falta de lesiones leves: nivel leve de daño psíquico.
b.	Lesiones leves: nivel moderado de daño psíquico.
c.	Lesiones graves: nivel grave o muy grave de daño psíquico”. (*)

(*) Confrontar con el Artículo 1 del Decreto Legislativo N° 1323, publicado el 06 enero 2017.

TERCERA. Modificación del artículo 242 del Código Procesal Penal
Modifícase el artículo 242 del Código Procesal Penal, promulgado por el Decreto Legislativo 957, el cual queda redactado en los términos siguientes:

“Artículo 242. Supuestos de prueba anticipada.-

1.	Durante la Investigación Preparatoria, a solicitud del Fiscal o de los demás sujetos procesales, podrá instarse al Juez de la Investigación Preparatoria actuación de una prueba anticipada, en los siguientes casos:
a)	Testimonial y examen del perito, cuando se requiera examinarlos con urgencia ante la presencia de un motivo fundado para considerar que no podrá hacerse en el juicio oral por enfermedad u otro grave impedimento, o que han sido expuestos a violencia, amenaza, ofertas o promesa de dinero u otra utilidad para que no declaren o lo hagan falsamente. El interrogatorio al perito, puede incluir el debate pericial cuando éste sea procedente.

b)	Careo entre las personas que han declarado, por los mismos motivos del literal anterior, siempre que se cumplan los requisitos establecidos en el artículo 182.
c)	Reconocimientos, inspecciones o reconstrucciones, que por su naturaleza y características deben ser considerados actos definitivos e irreproducibles, y no sea posible postergar su realización hasta la realización del juicio.

d)	Declaración de las niñas, niños y adolescentes en su calidad de agraviados por delitos comprendidos en los artículos 153 y 153-A del Capítulo I: Violación de la libertad personal, y en los comprendidos en el Capítulo IX: Violación de la libertad sexual, Capítulo X: Proxenetismo y Capítulo XI: Ofensas al pudor público, correspondientes al Título IV: Delitos contra la libertad, del Código Penal.

Las declaraciones de las niñas, niños y adolescentes serán realizadas con la intervención de psicólogos especializados en cámaras Gesell o salas de entrevistas implementadas por el Ministerio Público.
Las declaraciones y entrevistas serán filmadas y grabadas a fin de evitar la revictimización de los agraviados.

2.	Las mismas actuaciones de prueba podrán realizarse durante la etapa intermedia”. (*)

(*) Confrontar con el Artículo 2 del Decreto Legislativo N° 1307, publicado el 30 diciembre 2016, el mismo que entró en vigencia a nivel nacional a los noventa (90) días de su publicación en el diario oficial El Peruano.

CUARTA. Modificación del artículo 667 del Código Civil
Modifícase el artículo 667 del Código Civil, aprobado por el Decreto Legislativo 295, el cual queda redactado en los términos siguientes:

Article 124

B. Determination of psychological injury
The level of psychological injury is determined through an assessment carried out in accordance with the official specialized technical instrument that guides the expert work, with the following equivalence:

a.	Minor injury offense: mild level of psychological harm.
b.	Minor injuries: moderate level of psychological harm.

THIRD. Amendment of article 242 of the Criminal Procedure Code
Article 242 of the Criminal Procedure Code, enacted by Legislative Decree 957, is amended, which is worded as follows:

"Article 242. Cases of advance evidence.-

1.	During the Preparatory Investigation, at the request of the Prosecutor or other procedural parties, the Preparatory Investigation Judge may be requested to take advance evidence, in the following cases:
a)	Testimony and examination of the expert, when it is necessary to examine them urgently in the presence of a founded reason to consider that it cannot be done at the oral trial due to illness or other serious impediment, or that they have been exposed to violence, threat, offers or promise of money or other benefit so that they do not testify or do so falsely. The interrogation of the expert may include expert debate when this is appropriate.

b)	Confrontation between persons who have testified, for the same reasons as the previous paragraph, provided that the requirements established in article 182 are met.
c)	Recognitions, inspections or reconstructions, which by their nature and characteristics must be considered definitive and irreproducible acts, and it is not possible to postpone their performance until the trial takes place.

d)	Statement of girls, boys and adolescents in their capacity as victims of crimes included in articles 153 and 153-A of Chapter I: Violation of personal freedom, and those included in Chapter IX: Violation of sexual freedom, Chapter X: Procuring and Chapter XI: Offenses against public decency, corresponding to Title IV: Crimes against freedom, of the Criminal Code.

The statements of girls, boys and adolescents shall be made with the intervention of specialized psychologists in Gesell chambers or interview rooms implemented by the Public Prosecutor's Office.
The statements and interviews shall be filmed and recorded in order to avoid revictimization of the victims.

2.	The same evidentiary proceedings may be carried out during the intermediate stage". (*)

(*) Compare with Article 2 of Legislative Decree No. 1307, published on December 30, 2016, which entered into force nationwide ninety (90) days after its publication in the official gazette El Peruano.

heading: Article 667
text:
Artículo 667

Son excluidos de la sucesión de determinada persona, por indignidad, como herederos o legatarios:
1.	Los autores y cómplices de homicidio doloso o de su tentativa, cometidos contra la vida del causante, de sus ascendientes, descendientes o cónyuge. Esta causal de indignidad no desaparece por el indulto ni por la prescripción de la pena.

2.	Los que hubieran sido condenados por delito doloso cometido en agravio del causante o de alguna de las personas a las que se refiere el inciso anterior.
3.	Los que hubieran denunciado calumniosamente al causante por delito al que la ley sanciona con pena privativa de libertad.
4.	Los que hubieran empleado dolo o violencia para impedir al causante que otorgue testamento o para obligarle a hacerlo, o para que revoque total o parcialmente el otorgado.
5.	Los que destruyan, oculten, falsifiquen o alteren el testamento de la persona de cuya sucesión se trata y quienes, a sabiendas, hagan uso de un testamento falsificado.
6.	Los que hubieran sido sancionados con sentencia firme en más de una oportunidad en un proceso de violencia familiar en agravio del causante. (*)

(*) Confrontar (numeral 6) con la Segunda Disposición Complementaria Modificatoria de la Ley N° 30490, publicada el 21 julio 2016.
7.	Es indigno de suceder al hijo, el progenitor que no lo hubiera reconocido voluntariamente durante la minoría de edad o que no le haya prestado alimentos y asistencia conforme a sus posibilidades económicas, aun cuando haya alcanzado la mayoría de edad, si estuviera imposibilitado de procurarse sus propios recursos económicos. También es indigno de suceder al causante el pariente con vocación hereditaria o el cónyuge que no le haya prestado asistencia y alimentos cuando por ley estuviera obligado a hacerlo y se hubiera planteado como tal en la vía judicial”.

Article 667

The following are excluded from the succession of a determined person, by unworthiness, as heirs or legatees:
1. The perpetrators and accomplices of intentional homicide or its attempt, committed against the life of the decedent, their ascendants, descendants or spouse. This ground of unworthiness does not disappear by pardon or by prescription of the penalty.

2. Those who have been convicted of an intentional crime committed to the detriment of the decedent or any of the persons referred to in the preceding paragraph.
3. Those who have slanderously denounced the decedent for a crime for which the law sanctions with deprivation of liberty.
4. Those who have employed fraud or violence to prevent the decedent from granting a will or to compel them to do so, or to revoke in whole or in part the one granted.
5. Those who destroy, conceal, falsify or alter the will of the person whose succession is concerned and those who, knowingly, make use of a falsified will.
6. Those who have been sanctioned with a final judgment on more than one occasion in a family violence proceeding to the detriment of the decedent. (*)

(*) Compare (numeral 6) with the Second Complementary Modifying Provision of Law No. 30490, published on July 21, 2016.
7. Unworthy to succeed the child is the parent who has not voluntarily recognized them during minority or who has not provided them with food and assistance according to their economic possibilities, even when they have reached the age of majority, if they were unable to procure their own economic resources. Also unworthy to succeed the decedent is the relative with hereditary vocation or the spouse who has not provided them with assistance and food when by law they were obligated to do so and it had been raised as such in the judicial process.
